sentences.text:
Shri Ved Prakash Tiwari - Government
Advocate for the State.

Appellant has filed third application i.e. I.A. No.14341/2025 an application under Section 389(1) of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973/Section 430 for the Bhartiya Nagrik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS)
2023 for suspension of jail sentence and grant of bail.

2. Appellant has been convicted under Sections 344, 363, 366, 376(2)(E) of the Indian Penal Code and Section 5(I)/6 of the POCSO Act and sentenced to undergo R.I. for three years, R.I. for seven years, R.I. for ten years, R.I. for life and R.I. for life with fine of Rs.25,000/-, Rs.25,000/-,
Rs.25,000/-, Rs.25,000/- and Rs.25,000/- respectively, with default stipulations.
3. Learned counsel appearing for appellant submitted that act which is said to have been committed by appellant cannot be said to be rape.
Appellant and prosecutrix were in love relationship.
Appellant was young man aged about 22 years at the time of incident and prosecutrix was aged about 15 years.
She was consenting party.
Appellant was convicted and sentenced since prosecutrix was below the age of consent.
Considering the aforesaid facts and circumstances of the case, jail sentence of appellant may be suspended and he may be released on bail.
4. Learned Government Advocate appearing for State strongly opposed the application and submitted that prosecutrix is minor.
Her consent is immaterial.
FSL is positive.
Offence committed by appellant is heinous in nature, therefore, 2 CRA-10069-2019 appellant may not be released on bail.

5. Heard the counsel for the parties.
6.
As per prosecution story, appellant and prosecutrix were in love relationship.

sentences.text: On the date of incident, both of them eloped and later on, she was recovered and complaint of rape was lodged.
Prosecutrix has not clearly narrated the incident of rape in her statement (EX.P/3) recorded under Section 164 of the Cr.P.C. Dr. Manju Singh (PW-7) has also not given definite opinion of rape.

7. Considering the aforesaid facts and circumstances of the case and also the nature of offence and the manner in which same is said to have been done, I.A. No.14341/2025 for suspension of sentence and grant of bail, is allowed.

8. It is hereby directed that the custodial sentence awarded to the appellant shall remain suspended during the pendency of this appeal and he shall be released on bail subject on depositing the fine amount, if already not deposited and on his furnishing a bail bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rs.
Fifty Thousand Only) with two solvent sureties bond of the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court, for his appearance before the Registry of this Court on 15.06.2026 and on such other dates as may be fixed in this regard till final disposal of this appeal.
9. Certified copy as per rules.
(VISHAL DHAGAT)
